{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Deerskin / HDI Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — verified findings and redline positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. The dominant theme is omission rather than bad drafting: the Agreement is silent on indemnification, limitation of liability, insurance, IP ownership of the Site and deliverables, and post-termination transition and data return — all in a contract under which HDI designs, develops and hosts our Site and holds our Content, user information and order data. Section 9 ("Warranties") is limited to corporate authority representations and the Globix acknowledgement, and Section 10 (General Provisions) contains no risk-allocation language at all.

Two findings are critical and both are absences: there is no HDI indemnity of any kind (including for third-party IP infringement), and there is no liability cap or consequential-damages exclusion, leaving both Parties with unlimited exposure. We propose inserting a Vendor indemnity at the preferred level and a single mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with standard uncapped carve-outs.

The high-severity items are the commercial restraints that run against us. Section 6.1 imposes an open-ended exclusivity and field-of-use restriction covering Deerskin Products "and products substantially similar", plus HDI's exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand online, with no duration cap because the term auto-renews annually under Section 4.1 and no performance-based exit. Section 4.2 requires the Company, on any termination, to pay HDI 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 in eight quarterly instalments — an uncapped stipulated sum far exceeding three months' fees — while Section 4.1 gives HDI a self-dated mid-term walk-away and leaves us without an express convenience right. Section 10.3 is a binding-effect provision only, so HDI is free to assign, including to a competitor.

Three provisions are compliant and require no redline: there is no MFN burdening us, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment (fees are a pure revenue share above an $11,000 monthly threshold), and no non-solicitation covenant binding the Company. Section 10.5's choice of New York law also matches our preferred position; only venue is missing.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 8 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 9 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 10 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 11 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 12 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 15 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 16 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 18 | Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |

### Proposed positions on the open items

- **INDEMN (critical, missing).** Insert an HDI indemnity covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics, plus a narrow reciprocal indemnity from us limited to Company-provided Content and our own breach of law. We deliberately do not add the fallback 3x-fees super-cap, which would introduce a new limit on HDI's exposure in an agreement that currently has no cap at all.
- **LOL-CAP (critical, missing).** Insert a single mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with a mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion and uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP. Our payment obligations are expressly confirmed not to be damages subject to the cap. Placed as new Section 10.9, it survives under existing Section 10.7.
- **ASSIGN (high).** Add assignment mechanics after Section 10.3: our free assignment to affiliates and M&A successors; HDI assignment only with our consent, not unreasonably withheld, and never to a competitor; and express confirmation that our change of control gives HDI no termination right.
- **EXCLUSIVITY (high).** Redline Section 6.1 to the fallback: exclusivity confined to Deerskin Products, capped at twelve months from the Effective Date, terminating automatically on any HDI service-level or delivery-date failure. HDI's reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 benefits us and is untouched.
- **LD (high).** Recast the Section 4.2 Termination Payment as an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees and declared the sole liquidated amount payable by us. We prefer this surgical edit to deletion, which would leave the retained machinery in 4.2(b)–(c) and the Section 4 heading dangling; 4.2(b) (no payment if the amount is zero or less) and 4.2(c) (instalments) remain coherent and favour us.
- **NONCOMPETE (high).** Convert Section 6.1 into an express permission, removing the restriction on "products substantially similar" and HDI's exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand. Section 6.3, which restricts HDI, is untouched. Noted but not flagged: the Section 9(b) proviso requiring termination of the Globix hosting agreement is a sourcing condition rather than a restriction on the businesses or products we may operate or build.
- **T4C (high).** Add an express Company convenience right on ninety days' notice; fix HDI's Termination Date at the end of the then-current term; and cap the Termination Payment at three months of the Section 3.1 amounts so the ceiling is neither undefined nor arguably zero.
- **GOVLAW (medium).** New York law in Section 10.5 already matches our preference; add one sentence conferring exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County, preserving only temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
- **LICENSE (medium).** Extend the Section 1.4 access/use grant to our affiliates on written notice. Successor transfer is already available through Section 10.3; contractor coverage and perpetual/irrevocable wording are preferred-level only and not pursued.
- **RENEWAL (medium).** Shorten the Section 4.1 non-renewal window from 90 to 60 days (the fallback ceiling). Renewal is on existing terms with no price-increase mechanic, so the price-cap element is not triggered; the absence of a vendor renewal reminder is a preferred-level refinement only.
- **TRANSITION (medium, missing).** Insert a new Section 4.3: up to six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of our data in a standard machine-readable format within thirty days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion thereafter. Fallback: ninety days' assistance with the same thirty-day export.
- **WARRANTY (medium).** Insert the fallback warranty as new Section 9(c) — ninety days for the Site and software conforming to documentation, thirty days for the services — with repair, replacement or refund as our remedy. Placement preserves the Section 10.7 survival reference to Section 9.
- **AUDIT (low).** Section 3.4's notice, business-hours and cost provisions already meet or exceed the fallback; add a once-per-year cap on frequency. Independent-auditor and off-site refinements are not pursued as the clause is a records inspection only.
- **IP (low, missing).** Insert a new Section 5.5 granting us a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Site and other deliverables, with HDI retaining its generic tools and know-how and any HDI licence in our data limited to processing it solely to provide the services. Because HDI bears all development cost under Sections 1.2 and 1.6, we target this fallback rather than a full assignment.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points our playbook treats as walk-away territory and where we should not sign as drafted:

1. **No Vendor indemnity of any kind (INDEMN).** The complete absence of an HDI IP indemnity is walk-away territory. HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site, so an unindemnified third-party infringement claim lands entirely on us.
2. **No insurance covenant (INSURANCE).** HDI hosts and operates the Site, collects consumer orders and handles Company Content and user information (Sections 1.4, 1.5, 8.1). The absence of any cover for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory. We seek CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M where HDI processes Company data, statutory workers' compensation and certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
3. **Watch item — 90-day non-renewal window (RENEWAL).** This fails the 60-day fallback ceiling and sits at the edge of walk-away territory. We should not concede beyond 60 days.

For completeness: the assignment silence in Section 10.3 and the missing performance warranty in Section 9 are material deviations but not walk-away items — there is no blanket prohibition on our assignment, no HDI change-of-control termination right, and no "AS IS" disclaimer.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Confirm commercial mandate on the Section 6.1 exclusivity and the Section 4.2 Termination Payment.** These two clauses are the principal economic exposure: an indefinite restraint on our own brand and category, paired with an uncapped exit charge measured against trailing Net Sales. We need the business team's position on the twelve-month exclusivity cap and the three-month fee cap before we issue the redline.
2. **Issue the redline covering the two critical insertions first** (HDI indemnity; mutual liability cap as new Section 10.9), presented together so HDI sees the risk package as a whole.
3. **Bundle the remaining insertions as a single "missing standard terms" package** — insurance, IP licence in the deliverables and data, transition assistance and data return, performance warranty, and New York County venue — framed as gap-filling rather than renegotiation.
4. **Table the shorter mechanical edits together**: assignment mechanics after Section 10.3, the 60-day non-renewal window, the Section 1.4 affiliate extension, the express Company convenience right, and the once-per-year cap on HDI's inspection right.
5. **Confirm no counter-ask is needed on MFN, minimum commitments or non-solicitation.** These are compliant and we should not reopen them.
6. **Diligence the Globix interaction.** Section 9(b) requires termination of the Globix hosting agreement; we should confirm with the business team that this is achievable on the contemplated timetable before signature.
"}
